stories.teaser: A lizard dropped its tail 99 million years ago, and amber kept it
stories.headline: Tel Aviv University researchers find a 99-million-year-old lizard tail in amber, shed to escape danger
stories.why: Published in Palaeontologia Electronica; evidence the survival trick already existed 99 million years ago.
texts:
The oldest escape trick in the book.

Tel Aviv University researcher Dolev Fabrikant and colleagues studied a lizard tail preserved in amber about 99 million years old. Micro-CT scans showed a ring of muscle at the break, the same pattern living lizards form when they deliberately drop their tails. Published in Palaeontologia Electronica.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Fossils #Science

Lizards were already dropping their tails in the age of the dinosaurs.

A 99-million-year-old amber specimen, now in the Steinhardt Museum of Natural History at Tel Aviv University, preserves a detached lizard tail with skin and muscle. The researchers say genes involved in tail regeneration may have arisen by at least 99 million years ago.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Fossils #Science

Did it escape, or did a predator lose its meal?

Either way, a lizard tail landed in sticky tree resin about 99 million years ago. Tel Aviv University researchers scanned the amber and found the telltale muscle pattern of a deliberate tail drop, documenting a behavior, not just an anatomy, from the mid-Cretaceous.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Fossils #Science
stories.og_title: Lizard Dropped Its Tail 99 Million Years Ago, Amber Preserved Evidence

stories.teaser: Why our knees wear out: the trade-off behind the human brain
stories.headline: Weizmann Institute study in Nature links our flexible brains to our fragile knees
stories.why: A genome-wide study with Kyoto University points to a molecule behind both, and possible new osteoarthritis research.
texts:
Smart brains, weak knees.

Weizmann Institute researchers led by Dr. David Gokhman, with Kyoto University, found that humans make fewer GAGs, shock-absorbing molecules in joint cartilage that also stiffen brain connections. The result: flexible brains, but joints less able to absorb shocks. Published in Nature.

“We have a unique brain with high capabilities, but our fragile skeleton goes through degeneration very fast.”

#Israel #Weizmann #Evolution #Science

About 500,000 single-letter DNA differences separate humans from chimpanzees.

Weizmann Institute and Kyoto University scientists searched them for the ones that changed skeletal development, and found a gene group that is strongly silenced in humans. Published in Nature, the study could point toward new research on osteoarthritis, which affects hundreds of millions of people.

#Israel #Weizmann #Evolution #Science

“We can see step by step what evolution did, and we can also see diseases that emerged in our evolution,” says Dr. David Gokhman of the Weizmann Institute.

His team found that the same change that helps keep human brains flexible may also have made our joints less effective at absorbing shocks. The study was published in Nature.

#Israel #Weizmann #Evolution #Science
stories.og_title: Weak knees, smart brains: Israeli study gets to the bottom of genetic evolution

stories.teaser: Can crowds predict the future? A million forecasts say: pretty well
stories.headline: Tel Aviv University study of over a million forecasts finds crowds predict the future surprisingly well
stories.why: Published in PNAS; analyzed forecasts from four prediction platforms across 12 domains.
texts:
Can we really predict the future?

Tel Aviv University researchers led by Prof. Michael Gilead analyzed 1,014,122 forecasts from four prediction platforms, covering a decade of elections, technology, geopolitics and more. Crowd forecasts matched reality well: events given a 70% chance happened about 70% of the time. Published in PNAS.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Psychology #Science

Events given a 70% chance of happening occurred approximately 70% of the time.

That’s what Tel Aviv University psychologists found after studying over a million crowd forecasts from Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold and Metaculus. Forecasts were already well calibrated after just 25% of their forecasting period. The researchers stress this doesn’t mean anyone can predict the future with certainty.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Psychology #Science

A million predictions, put to the test.

Prof. Michael Gilead’s team at Tel Aviv University checked forecasts across 12 domains against what actually happened. Crowds were well calibrated overall, though they tended to overestimate events in technology and international relations and underestimate election-related ones. The study was published in PNAS.

#Israel #TelAvivUniversity #Psychology #Science
stories.og_title: Can We Really Predict the Future?

stories.teaser: Six Israeli researchers join Cornell through a new exchange
stories.headline: Cornell launches an Israeli scholar exchange, welcoming six researchers from Jewish and Arab communities
stories.why: The Kalaniyot chapter at Cornell hosts Israeli postdocs and sabbatical scholars in fields from gut health to quantum computing.
texts:
Six Israeli scientists, one American campus.

Cornell University launched a Kalaniyot chapter, hosting three postdoctoral fellows and three sabbatical scholars from Israel’s Jewish and Arab communities. Their work ranges from gut health and wetlands to detecting plant disease and trapped-ion quantum computing.

“Anyone with a Ph.D. from an Israeli university, or a faculty position at one, can apply.”

#Israel #Cornell #Science #Kalaniyot

From ponds to quantum sensors.

Israeli hydrologist Ohad Shalom is studying ponds and wetlands at Cornell. Loai Basheer is looking at how the spotted lanternfly affects grape products, and Ori Katz is working on trapped-ion quantum computing. They are part of the first cohort of Cornell’s new Kalaniyot chapter for Israeli scholars.

#Israel #Cornell #Science #Kalaniyot

Science keeps building bridges.

Cornell’s new Kalaniyot chapter, one of seven in the US, brings Israeli researchers to campus. Its first six scholars, from both Jewish and Arab communities, are working with Cornell faculty on nutrition, ecology, plant disease, developmental science and quantum physics. Cornell said religion and ethnicity are not considered in selection.

#Israel #Cornell #Science #Kalaniyot
stories.og_title: Cornell launches Israeli scholar exchange with six researchers on campus

stories.teaser: How soaring birds fly on almost free energy
stories.headline: University of Haifa researchers reveal how soaring birds fly on “free fuel” from the sky
stories.why: Published in Science; based on GPS data from 850 birds and bats of 38 species collected over 17 years.
texts:
Free fuel from the sky.

An international study with University of Haifa researchers found that soaring on air currents costs less energy per distance than flapping. An Andean condor needed about 79% less energy per kilometer than a trumpeter swan of similar weight. Published in Science.

“The air is not only the space in which birds fly, but also a source of energy for them,” says Dr. Yuval Werber.

#Israel #UniversityOfHaifa #Birds #Science

Flapping just 0.1% of the time.

That’s how little an Andean condor flaps in flight, compared with about 99% for a trumpeter swan of the same weight. Researchers including Dr. Yuval Werber and Prof. Nir Sapir of the University of Haifa analyzed GPS and accelerometer data from 850 birds and bats of 38 species, collected over 17 years. Published in Science.

#Israel #UniversityOfHaifa #Birds #Science

Seven vulture species, more than 4.3 million kilometers.

That’s enough to circle the Earth more than 100 times, and they flapped for only 0.1% to 7% of it. A study published in Science, with University of Haifa researchers, shows how soaring birds draw energy from air currents, and why their flight can cost less than flapping.

#Israel #UniversityOfHaifa #Birds #Science
stories.og_title: השמיים הם הגבול, והאנרגיה בחינם: סוד התעופה החסכונית של העופות הדואים

stories.teaser: A red alga thrives in near-darkness in Rosh HaNikra’s sea caves
stories.headline: Israeli researchers find a red alga thriving in near-total darkness in the Rosh HaNikra sea caves
stories.why: Published in Aquatic Sciences; part of a 2019–2022 survey of Israel’s coast.
texts:
Life in the dark.

In the sea caves of Rosh HaNikra, where light is just 0.5% to 2.5% of what it is outside, Israeli researchers found the red alga Hildenbrandia rubra photosynthesizing efficiently. Led by Prof. David Iluz of Beit Berl Academic College with the University of Haifa, the study was published in Aquatic Sciences.

#Israel #RoshHaNikra #MarineLife #Science

“We tend to think of caves as environments where living conditions are limited,” says Prof. David Iluz.

But in the Rosh HaNikra sea caves, his team found a red alga growing on the walls in almost total darkness, alongside other algae and photosynthetic bacteria forming a colorful, complex ecosystem. The researchers say sea caves are refuges for sensitive species.

#Israel #RoshHaNikra #MarineLife #Science

A colorful world hidden in the dark.

During a survey of Israel’s coast from Ashdod to Rosh HaNikra, researchers from Beit Berl, the University of Haifa, Bar-Ilan and other institutions found a red alga that thrives on cave walls with barely any light. Its reproduction peaks in autumn and early winter.

#Israel #RoshHaNikra #MarineLife #Science
stories.og_title: תגלית בגבול לבנון: האצה האדומה ששורדת בחושך כמעט מוחלט

stories.teaser: Intel agrees to buy Israeli quantum software company Classiq
stories.headline: Intel agrees to buy Israeli quantum computing company Classiq, its biggest Israeli acquisition since Mobileye
stories.why: Classiq makes software that lets developers build quantum applications without deep quantum expertise.
texts:
Israeli quantum software, going big.

Intel has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Classiq, an Israeli company whose platform lets developers build quantum computing applications without deep quantum circuit design expertise. Globes reported the price at $2.2 billion, which would make it Intel’s largest Israeli acquisition since Mobileye.

“Classiq has focused on making quantum computing practical and accessible,” says CEO Nir Minerbi.

#Israel #Classiq #QuantumComputing #Tech

“Joining forces with Classiq transforms Intel’s Quantum Computing Group into a full-stack quantum computing business,” says Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan.

Intel has agreed to acquire Israel’s Classiq, whose software works across different quantum hardware. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

#Israel #Classiq #QuantumComputing #Tech

How do you program a quantum computer?

Israeli company Classiq built a platform that makes it far easier, and now Intel has agreed to buy it. Intel plans to keep supporting Classiq’s integrations with multiple quantum hardware platforms. Globes reported the deal at $2.2 billion, the biggest Israeli acquisition for Intel since Mobileye in 2017.

#Israel #Classiq #QuantumComputing #Tech
stories.og_title: Intel agrees to buy Classiq in biggest Israeli acquisition since Mobileye

stories.teaser: A butterfly that crosses continents in a relay through Israel
stories.headline: Israeli volunteers and researchers track a butterfly that migrates across continents in a generational relay
stories.why: Based on a decade of Israel’s National Butterfly Monitoring Program, run largely by volunteers.
texts:
A migration passed from generation to generation.

The Southern Festoon butterfly doesn’t make its long journey alone. It travels in a relay, one generation after another, following warmth and the caper plants its caterpillars feed on. Tel Aviv University PhD student Eyal Simons studies it using data from Israel’s volunteer-run National Butterfly Monitoring Program.

#Israel #Butterflies #CitizenScience #Nature

Butterflies are a “thermometer of nature.”

Over a decade, Israeli researchers compared 20 butterfly species using data gathered by volunteers. Heat-loving African species expanded their range, while species from Europe and Asia declined. One clear winner: the Southern Festoon, which migrates in a relay across generations and now sometimes spends the winter across most of Israel.

#Israel #Butterflies #CitizenScience #Nature

Each female lays about 150 to 200 eggs, one at a time, on caper leaves.

That’s how the Southern Festoon butterfly keeps its multi-generation migration going. Volunteers with the Israel Butterfly Lovers Society and the Israeli Citizen Science Center help track it, and a Tel Aviv University study is now following how it responds to warming winters.

#Israel #Butterflies #CitizenScience #Nature
stories.og_title: הפרפר שחוצה יבשות במרוץ שליחים דרך ישראל

stories.teaser: A 3,200-year-old fortress from the time of the Judges reopens
stories.headline: The restored 3,200-year-old Galon Fortress opens to visitors in the Beit Guvrin Forest
stories.why: Restored by KKL-JNF and the Israel Antiquities Authority, now with accessible paths and new signage.
texts:
Step back 3,200 years.

The restored Galon Fortress in the Beit Guvrin Forest, dating to the mid-12th century BCE, has been inaugurated by KKL-JNF and the Israel Antiquities Authority. Overlooking the main road between the coastal plain and the Judean Shephelah, it offers a glimpse of the world described in the Book of Judges.

#Israel #Archaeology #History #IsraelAntiquities

An ancient fortress, now open to everyone.

The 3,200-year-old Galon Fortress near Beit Guvrin has been conserved and restored, with an access road, picnic area, accessible parking, an accessible path and new signage. Dozens of young people and volunteers took part in the excavation, led by Dr. Saar Ganor and Dr. Itamar Weissbein of the Israel Antiquities Authority.

#Israel #Archaeology #History #IsraelAntiquities

“Preserving the heritage sites of the Land of Israel is part of our connection to our roots,” says KKL-JNF chairman Eyal Ostrinsky.

The Galon Fortress, from the period of the Judges, has reopened in the Beit Guvrin Forest after conservation work. Vessels about 3,200 years old were found during the excavation, and the site is now accessible to people with disabilities.

#Israel #Archaeology #History #IsraelAntiquities
stories.og_title: נחנכה מצודת גלאון המחודשת: הצצה למאבקים בארץ לפני כ-3,200 שנה

stories.headline: Israel’s volunteer wildlife rescue network celebrates 10 years and about 55,500 calls
stories.why: Hundreds of volunteers rescue injured and orphaned wild animals across the country.
texts:
A decade of kindness for wild animals.

Israel’s volunteer wildlife rescue network, known as “Hivbulans,” is marking 10 years. Its roughly 250 active volunteers, working with about 40 transit stations trained in animal first aid, have handled about 55,500 reports and calls. An estimated 65–70% of treated wild animals survive.

#Israel #Wildlife #Volunteers #AnimalRescue

1,476 hedgehog calls in 2025 alone.

Hedgehogs make up about 30% of the reports to Israel’s volunteer wildlife rescue network, which just turned 10. Over the decade, about 1,000 volunteers have helped rescue injured and orphaned animals, from buzzards to tortoises and chameleons.

“Since then I’ve rescued more than 15 wild animals,” says volunteer Marwa Oda.

#Israel #Wildlife #Volunteers #AnimalRescue

“One of the most moving cases was reuniting Ofer with his mother, after mushroom pickers mistakenly took him along,” says volunteer Amit Almog.

Almog is one of about 250 active volunteers in Israel’s wildlife rescue network, which is celebrating 10 years. Together they have answered about 55,500 calls for injured and orphaned wild animals.

#Israel #Wildlife #Volunteers #AnimalRescue
stories.og_title: עשור של חסד: החיבולנס חוגג 10 שנים

stories.teaser: AI and satellites map every farm plot in Israel
stories.headline: An Israeli AI system maps about 200,000 farm plots from space, revealing how Israel’s agriculture is changing
stories.why: Developed with the Volcani Institute and Ben-Gurion University, it replaces costly manual surveys.
texts:
Israel’s farms, mapped from space.

Israel’s Ministry of Agriculture developed an AI system that uses satellite and aerial imagery to automatically map about 200,000 farm plots and track crop growth in near real time. Built over three years with the Volcani Institute and Ben-Gurion University, it recognizes more than 40 crops.

#Israel #AgTech #AI #Agriculture

Avocado orchards up 56%. Vineyards up 22%.

A new Israeli AI system that reads satellite images of about 200,000 farm plots shows how Israel’s agriculture changed from 2018 to 2025. Avocado area grew from about 116,000 to about 181,000 dunams, and corn in the Negev grew by about 25,000 dunams.

#Israel #AgTech #AI #Agriculture

“The system was originally designed to identify 28 main crops, but was ultimately expanded to more than 40,” says Dr. Ofer Rosenstein of the Volcani Institute.

The Israeli AI tool, built with Ben-Gurion University researchers, maps farm plots from satellite images in near real time, replacing surveys that cost over 2 million shekels each.

#Israel #AgTech #AI #Agriculture
stories.og_title: AI וצילומי לוויין חושפים: יותר אבוקדו וגפנים בישראל, פחות חומוס

stories.teaser: An Israeli hospital gives a new non-invasive epilepsy treatment
stories.headline: Beilinson Hospital gives a non-invasive brain stimulation treatment for epilepsy, the first outside Europe
stories.why: The EASEE system stimulates the brain from outside the skull, with no brain surgery or electrodes.
texts:
Treating epilepsy without entering the brain.

At Clalit-Beilinson Hospital, Olga Moisa, 42, who has lived with epilepsy for 15 years, became the first patient outside Europe to receive the EASEE system, which stimulates the brain from outside the skull. She has had no seizures since, though doctors say it is too early to judge.

#Israel #Beilinson #Epilepsy #Health

“This is the first time we can treat patients with epilepsy without penetrating the brain,” says Dr. Idit Tamir of Beilinson Hospital.

Tamir’s team gave the first treatment outside Europe with EASEE, a brain stimulation system that needs no craniotomy and no brain electrodes. About a third of Israel’s 100,000 people with epilepsy don’t get adequate seizure control from medication.

#Israel #Beilinson #Epilepsy #Health

“Even if there is something that can reduce the seizures by 50%, that is already better,” says Sasha, the son of Olga Moisa.

His mother, 42, became the first patient outside Europe to receive EASEE, a non-invasive brain stimulation system for epilepsy, at Beilinson Hospital. It is too early to judge the results, but she has had no seizures since.

#Israel #Beilinson #Epilepsy #Health
stories.og_title: New non-invasive epilepsy treatment given to first Israeli patient
